Split the input on newlines and drop the empty tail a trailing newline leaves. From each line strip the leading spaces and tabs; ignore the line when nothing is left or when what is left begins with `#`. Otherwise the address runs to the next space or tab or to the end of the line, one run of spaces and tabs is skipped, and the rest of the line, verbatim, is the cell's content. Exit 0 whenever the sheet parses.

An address is one or two letters naming a column and one to three digits naming a row, upper-cased when read, so `a1` and `A1` are one cell; columns run `A` to `Z` and then `AA` to `ZZ`, and the row is at least 1. Cells print in ascending column order and, within a column, ascending row order.

Content that begins with `=` is a formula; anything else is a literal. A literal that is empty, or a cell nobody declared, is the number 0. A literal that matches an optional `-`, digits, and optionally a `.` and more digits is that number. A literal that is exactly one of the error tokens `#DIV/0!`, `#REF!`, `#VALUE!`, `#CYCLE!`, `#NAME?` and `#ERR!` is that error. Everything else is text.

A formula body holds numbers written as digits with an optional `.` and more digits and no sign and no exponent, cell addresses, ranges written `A1:B3`, the bare words `TRUE` and `FALSE`, function calls, parentheses, and the operators `^`, `*`, `/`, `+`, `-`, `=`, `<>`, `<`, `<=`, `>` and `>=`. Spaces and tabs may sit anywhere between tokens. Names are read case-insensitively. Precedence, loosest first, is the comparisons, then `+` and `-`, then `*` and `/`, then `^`, and then a leading `-` or `+`; the comparisons and the additive and multiplicative operators group to the left, `^` groups to the right, and a leading sign binds tighter than `^`, so `-2^2` is 4 and `2^3^2` is 512. Anything the grammar does not accept makes the cell `#ERR!`, and so does a range written anywhere but directly as a function argument, which the grammar does accept. A word the grammar accepts that is neither `TRUE`, `FALSE` nor the name of a call is read as a cell address, and one that is not one or two letters and one to three digits naming a row of at least 1 — `AAA1`, `A1000`, `A0` and `FOO` alike — is an address outside the addressable range rather than a grammar failure.

The functions are `SUM`, `MIN`, `MAX`, `COUNT` and `AVG`, each taking one or more arguments, `ABS` taking exactly one, and `IF` taking exactly three. A call with the wrong number of arguments is `#ERR!` and a call to any other name is `#NAME?`. An argument that is a range contributes every cell it covers, in ascending column and then ascending row order, whichever corner it was written from. `SUM` totals, `MIN` and `MAX` pick, `AVG` totals and divides by how many values it saw, and `COUNT` reports how many of its values are numbers. Every one of them but `COUNT` reads each value it takes as a number, so `ABS`, `SUM`, `MIN`, `MAX` and `AVG` take text as `#VALUE!` rather than ordering or ignoring it. `IF` reads its first argument as a condition, taking `TRUE` and a non-zero number as true and `FALSE` and zero as false, and returns only the branch it takes, so an error in the other branch is invisible.

A value is a number, text, a boolean, or an error. In an arithmetic position a boolean is 1 or 0 and text is `#VALUE!`. Division by a zero divisor is `#DIV/0!`, and so is any arithmetic result that is not finite. A comparison compares two numbers numerically, two texts by code point, and two booleans with false below true; across kinds every number is below every text and every text is below every boolean. An address outside the addressable range is `#REF!`. A cell whose evaluation reaches itself, directly or through other cells, is `#CYCLE!`. An error reaching an operator or a function is the result: for an operator the left operand's error wins over the right one's, and for a function the first error among the arguments read left to right, ranges expanded, wins over everything else, including over `COUNT` counting.

88: class Tokenizer {
89:   constructor(input) {
90:     this.input = input
91:     this.pos = 0
92:   }
93: 
94:   skipWhitespace() {
95:     while (this.pos < this.input.length && /[ \t]/.test(this.input[this.pos])) {
96:       this.pos++
97:     }
98:   }
99: 
100:   peek() {
101:     this.skipWhitespace()
102:     return this.pos < this.input.length ? this.input[this.pos] : null
103:   }
104: 
105:   peekN(n) {
106:     let tmp = this.pos
107:     this.skipWhitespace()
108:     let result = ''
109:     while (n-- > 0 && this.pos < this.input.length) {
110:       result += this.input[this.pos++]
111:     }
112:     this.pos = tmp
113:     return result
114:   }
115: 
116:   next() {
117:     this.skipWhitespace()
118:     if (this.pos >= this.input.length) return null
119: 
120:     const ch = this.input[this.pos]
121: 
122:     // Numbers
123:     if (/\d/.test(ch)) {
124:       let num = ''
125:       while (this.pos < this.input.length && /[\d.]/.test(this.input[this.pos])) {
126:         num += this.input[this.pos++]
127:       }
128:       return { type: 'number', val: parseFloat(num) }
129:     }
130: 
131:     // Cell addresses or keywords (letters)
132:     if (/[A-Za-z]/.test(ch)) {
133:       let word = ''
134:       while (this.pos < this.input.length && /[A-Za-z0-9]/.test(this.input[this.pos])) {
135:         word += this.input[this.pos++]
136:       }
137:       const upper = word.toUpperCase()
138:       if (upper === 'TRUE') return { type: 'boolean', val: true }
139:       if (upper === 'FALSE') return { type: 'boolean', val: false }
140:       if (/^[A-Z]{1,2}\d{1,3}$/.test(upper)) return { type: 'address', val: upper }
141:       return { type: 'name', val: upper }
142:     }
143: 
144:     // Operators and punctuation
145:     if (ch === ':') {
146:       this.pos++
147:       return { type: 'colon' }
148:     }
149:     if (ch === '(') {
150:       this.pos++
151:       return { type: 'lparen' }
152:     }
153:     if (ch === ')') {
154:       this.pos++
155:       return { type: 'rparen' }
156:     }
157:     if (ch === ',') {
158:       this.pos++
159:       return { type: 'comma' }
160:     }
161:     if (ch === '+') {
162:       this.pos++
163:       return { type: 'plus' }
164:     }
165:     if (ch === '-') {
166:       this.pos++
167:       return { type: 'minus' }
168:     }
169:     if (ch === '*') {
170:       this.pos++
171:       return { type: 'mul' }
172:     }
173:     if (ch === '/') {
174:       this.pos++
175:       return { type: 'div' }
176:     }
177:     if (ch === '^') {
178:       this.pos++
179:       return { type: 'pow' }
180:     }
181:     if (ch === '=') {
182:       this.pos++
183:       return { type: 'eq' }
184:     }
185:     if (ch === '<') {
186:       this.pos++
187:       if (this.pos < this.input.length && this.input[this.pos] === '=') {
188:         this.pos++
189:         return { type: 'lte' }
190:       }
191:       if (this.pos < this.input.length && this.input[this.pos] === '>') {
192:         this.pos++
193:         return { type: 'neq' }
194:       }
195:       return { type: 'lt' }
196:     }
197:     if (ch === '>') {
198:       this.pos++
199:       if (this.pos < this.input.length && this.input[this.pos] === '=') {
200:         this.pos++
201:         return { type: 'gte' }
202:       }
203:       return { type: 'gt' }
204:     }
205: 
206:     // Unknown character
207:     return null
208:   }
209: }

211: class Parser {
212:   constructor(formula) {
213:     this.tokenizer = new Tokenizer(formula)
214:     this.current = this.tokenizer.next()
215:   }
216: 
217:   advance() {
218:     this.current = this.tokenizer.next()
219:   }
220: 
221:   expect(type) {
222:     if (!this.current || this.current.type !== type) {
223:       throw new Error(ERROR_ERR)
224:     }
225:     const token = this.current
226:     this.advance()
227:     return token
228:   }
229: 
230:   parse() {
231:     const expr = this.parseComparison()
232:     if (this.current !== null) {
233:       throw new Error(ERROR_ERR)
234:     }
235:     return expr
236:   }
237: 
238:   parseComparison() {
239:     let left = this.parseAdditive()
240:     while (this.current && ['eq', 'neq', 'lt', 'lte', 'gt', 'gte'].includes(this.current.type)) {
241:       const op = this.current.type
242:       this.advance()
243:       const right = this.parseAdditive()
244:       left = { type: 'comparison', op, left, right }
245:     }
246:     return left
247:   }
248: 
249:   parseAdditive() {
250:     let left = this.parseMultiplicative()
251:     while (this.current && ['plus', 'minus'].includes(this.current.type)) {
252:       const op = this.current.type
253:       this.advance()
254:       const right = this.parseMultiplicative()
255:       left = { type: 'binary', op, left, right }
256:     }
257:     return left
258:   }
259: 
260:   parseMultiplicative() {
261:     let left = this.parsePower()
262:     while (this.current && ['mul', 'div'].includes(this.current.type)) {
263:       const op = this.current.type
264:       this.advance()
265:       const right = this.parsePower()
266:       left = { type: 'binary', op, left, right }
267:     }
268:     return left
269:   }
270: 
271:   parsePower() {
272:     let left = this.parseUnary()
273:     if (this.current && this.current.type === 'pow') {
274:       this.advance()
275:       const right = this.parsePower() // Right associative
276:       left = { type: 'binary', op: 'pow', left, right }
277:     }
278:     return left
279:   }
280: 
281:   parseUnary() {
282:     if (this.current && ['plus', 'minus'].includes(this.current.type)) {
283:       const op = this.current.type
284:       this.advance()
285:       const expr = this.parseUnary()
286:       return { type: 'unary', op, expr }
287:     }
288:     return this.parsePrimary()
289:   }
290: 
291:   parsePrimary() {
292:     if (!this.current) {
293:       throw new Error(ERROR_ERR)
294:     }
295: 
296:     if (this.current.type === 'lparen') {
297:       this.advance()
298:       const expr = this.parseComparison()
299:       this.expect('rparen')
300:       return expr
301:     }
302: 
303:     if (this.current.type === 'number') {
304:       const val = this.current.val
305:       this.advance()
306:       return { type: 'number', val }
307:     }
308: 
309:     if (this.current.type === 'boolean') {
310:       const val = this.current.val
311:       this.advance()
312:       return { type: 'boolean', val }
313:     }
314: 
315:     if (this.current.type === 'address') {
316:       const addr = this.current.val
317:       this.advance()
318: 
319:       // Check for range
320:       if (this.current && this.current.type === 'colon') {
321:         this.advance()
322:         if (!this.current || this.current.type !== 'address') {
323:           throw new Error(ERROR_ERR)
324:         }
325:         const addr2 = this.current.val
326:         this.advance()
327:         return { type: 'range', addr1: addr, addr2 }
328:       }
329: 
330:       return { type: 'address', val: addr }
331:     }
332: 
333:     if (this.current.type === 'name') {
334:       const name = this.current.val
335:       this.advance()
336: 
337:       // Function call
338:       if (this.current && this.current.type === 'lparen') {
339:         this.advance()
340:         const args = []
341:         if (this.current && this.current.type !== 'rparen') {
342:           args.push(this.parseComparison())
343:           while (this.current && this.current.type === 'comma') {
344:             this.advance()
345:             args.push(this.parseComparison())
346:           }
347:         }
348:         this.expect('rparen')
349:         return { type: 'call', name, args }
350:       }
351: 
352:       // Bare name is treated as address but invalid
353:       return { type: 'address', val: name }
354:     }
355: 
356:     throw new Error(ERROR_ERR)
357:   }
358: }

360: class Evaluator {
361:   constructor(cells) {
362:     this.cells = cells
363:     this.cache = new Map()
364:     this.evaluating = new Set()
365:   }
366: 
367:   evaluate(addr) {
368:     if (this.cache.has(addr)) {
369:       return this.cache.get(addr)
370:     }
371: 
372:     if (this.evaluating.has(addr)) {
373:       return Value.error(ERROR_CYCLE)
374:     }
375: 
376:     this.evaluating.add(addr)
377: 
378:     const cell = this.cells.get(addr)
379:     let result
380: 
381:     if (!cell) {
382:       result = Value.zero()
383:     } else {
384:       const content = parseContent(cell.content)
385:       if (content.type === 'formula') {
386:         try {
387:           const parser = new Parser(content.formula)
388:           const ast = parser.parse()
389:           result = this.evaluateAst(ast)
390:         } catch (e) {
391:           result = Value.error(e.message.startsWith('#') ? e.message : ERROR_ERR)
392:         }
393:       } else {
394:         result = content
395:       }
396:     }
397: 
398:     this.evaluating.delete(addr)
399:     this.cache.set(addr, result)
400:     return result
401:   }
402: 
403:   evaluateAst(node) {
404:     if (!node) return Value.error(ERROR_ERR)
405: 
406:     if (node.type === 'number') {
407:       return Value.number(node.val)
408:     }
409: 
410:     if (node.type === 'boolean') {
411:       return Value.boolean(node.val)
412:     }
413: 
414:     if (node.type === 'address') {
415:       const parsed = parseAddress(node.val)
416:       if (!parsed) {
417:         return Value.error(ERROR_REF)
418:       }
419:       const addr = addressToString(parsed.col, parsed.row)
420:       return this.evaluate(addr)
421:     }
422: 
423:     if (node.type === 'range') {
424:       return Value.error(ERROR_ERR) // Ranges should only appear as function arguments
425:     }
426: 
427:     if (node.type === 'binary') {
428:       const left = this.evaluateAst(node.left)
429:       if (left.isError()) return left
430: 
431:       const right = this.evaluateAst(node.right)
432:       if (right.isError()) return right
433: 
434:       return this.evaluateBinary(node.op, left, right)
435:     }
436: 
437:     if (node.type === 'comparison') {
438:       const left = this.evaluateAst(node.left)
439:       if (left.isError()) return left
440: 
441:       const right = this.evaluateAst(node.right)
442:       if (right.isError()) return right
443: 
444:       return this.evaluateComparison(node.op, left, right)
445:     }
446: 
447:     if (node.type === 'unary') {
448:       const expr = this.evaluateAst(node.expr)
449:       if (expr.isError()) return expr
450: 
451:       if (node.op === 'minus') {
452:         const num = expr.asNumber()
453:         if (num.isError()) return num
454:         return Value.number(-num.val)
455:       } else { // plus
456:         const num = expr.asNumber()
457:         if (num.isError()) return num
458:         return Value.number(num.val)
459:       }
460:     }
461: 
462:     if (node.type === 'call') {
463:       return this.evaluateCall(node.name, node.args)
464:     }
465: 
466:     return Value.error(ERROR_ERR)
467:   }

469:   evaluateBinary(op, left, right) {
470:     if (op === 'plus') {
471:       const l = left.asNumber()
472:       if (l.isError()) return l
473:       const r = right.asNumber()
474:       if (r.isError()) return r
475:       const result = l.val + r.val
476:       if (!isFinite(result)) return Value.error(ERROR_DIV_ZERO)
477:       return Value.number(result)
478:     }
479: 
480:     if (op === 'minus') {
481:       const l = left.asNumber()
482:       if (l.isError()) return l
483:       const r = right.asNumber()
484:       if (r.isError()) return r
485:       const result = l.val - r.val
486:       if (!isFinite(result)) return Value.error(ERROR_DIV_ZERO)
487:       return Value.number(result)
488:     }
489: 
490:     if (op === 'mul') {
491:       const l = left.asNumber()
492:       if (l.isError()) return l
493:       const r = right.asNumber()
494:       if (r.isError()) return r
495:       const result = l.val * r.val
496:       if (!isFinite(result)) return Value.error(ERROR_DIV_ZERO)
497:       return Value.number(result)
498:     }
499: 
500:     if (op === 'div') {
501:       const l = left.asNumber()
502:       if (l.isError()) return l
503:       const r = right.asNumber()
504:       if (r.isError()) return r
505:       if (r.val === 0) return Value.error(ERROR_DIV_ZERO)
506:       const result = l.val / r.val
507:       if (!isFinite(result)) return Value.error(ERROR_DIV_ZERO)
508:       return Value.number(result)
509:     }
510: 
511:     if (op === 'pow') {
512:       const l = left.asNumber()
513:       if (l.isError()) return l
514:       const r = right.asNumber()
515:       if (r.isError()) return r
516:       const result = Math.pow(l.val, r.val)
517:       if (!isFinite(result)) return Value.error(ERROR_DIV_ZERO)
518:       return Value.number(result)
519:     }
520: 
521:     return Value.error(ERROR_ERR)
522:   }
523: 
524:   evaluateComparison(op, left, right) {
525:     // Determine types and convert if needed
526:     let cmp
527:     if (left.type === 'number' && right.type === 'number') {
528:       cmp = left.val < right.val ? -1 : left.val > right.val ? 1 : 0
529:     } else if (left.type === 'text' && right.type === 'text') {
530:       cmp = left.val < right.val ? -1 : left.val > right.val ? 1 : 0
531:     } else if (left.type === 'boolean' && right.type === 'boolean') {
532:       cmp = (left.val ? 1 : 0) < (right.val ? 1 : 0) ? -1 : (left.val ? 1 : 0) > (right.val ? 1 : 0) ? 1 : 0
533:     } else {
534:       // Different types: number < text < boolean
535:       const order = { number: 0, text: 1, boolean: 2 }
536:       const lo = order[left.type]
537:       const ro = order[right.type]
538:       cmp = lo < ro ? -1 : lo > ro ? 1 : 0
539:     }
540: 
541:     let result
542:     if (op === 'eq') result = cmp === 0
543:     else if (op === 'neq') result = cmp !== 0
544:     else if (op === 'lt') result = cmp < 0
545:     else if (op === 'lte') result = cmp <= 0
546:     else if (op === 'gt') result = cmp > 0
547:     else if (op === 'gte') result = cmp >= 0
548:     else return Value.error(ERROR_ERR)
549: 
550:     return Value.boolean(result)

553:   getRangeValues(node) {
554:     if (node.type === 'range') {
555:       const p1 = parseAddress(node.addr1)
556:       const p2 = parseAddress(node.addr2)
557:       if (!p1 || !p2) return []
558: 
559:       const col1 = p1.col.charCodeAt(0) - 'A'.charCodeAt(0)
560:       const col2 = p2.col.charCodeAt(0) - 'A'.charCodeAt(0)
561:       let c1, c2
562: 
563:       if (p1.col.length === 2) {
564:         c1 = 26 + (p1.col.charCodeAt(1) - 'A'.charCodeAt(0))
565:       } else {
566:         c1 = col1
567:       }
568: 
569:       if (p2.col.length === 2) {
570:         c2 = 26 + (p2.col.charCodeAt(1) - 'A'.charCodeAt(0))
571:       } else {
572:         c2 = col2
573:       }
574: 
575:       const minC = Math.min(c1, c2)
576:       const maxC = Math.max(c1, c2)
577:       const minR = Math.min(p1.row, p2.row)
578:       const maxR = Math.max(p1.row, p2.row)
579: 
580:       const values = []
581:       for (let c = minC; c <= maxC; c++) {
582:         for (let r = minR; r <= maxR; r++) {
583:           const col = c < 26 ? String.fromCharCode(c + 'A'.charCodeAt(0)) : 'A' + String.fromCharCode(c - 26 + 'A'.charCodeAt(0))
584:           const addr = col + r
585:           values.push(this.evaluate(addr))
586:         }
587:       }
588:       return values
589:     }
590: 
591:     return [this.evaluateAst(node)]
592:   }

594:   evaluateCall(name, args) {
595:     if (name === 'SUM') {
596:       if (args.length === 0) return Value.error(ERROR_ERR)
597:       const values = []
598:       for (const arg of args) {
599:         const v = this.getRangeValues(arg)
600:         if (v.some(x => x.isError())) {
601:           for (const val of v) {
602:             if (val.isError()) return val
603:           }
604:         }
605:         values.push(...v)
606:       }
607:       let sum = 0
608:       for (const val of values) {
609:         const num = val.asNumber()
610:         if (num.isError()) return num
611:         sum += num.val
612:       }
613:       return Value.number(sum)
614:     }
615: 
616:     if (name === 'MIN') {
617:       if (args.length === 0) return Value.error(ERROR_ERR)
618:       let min = Infinity
619:       for (const arg of args) {
620:         const v = this.getRangeValues(arg)
621:         if (v.some(x => x.isError())) {
622:           for (const val of v) {
623:             if (val.isError()) return val
624:           }
625:         }
626:         for (const val of v) {
627:           const num = val.asNumber()
628:           if (num.isError()) return num
629:           min = Math.min(min, num.val)
630:         }
631:       }
632:       return Value.number(min === Infinity ? 0 : min)
633:     }
634: 
635:     if (name === 'MAX') {
636:       if (args.length === 0) return Value.error(ERROR_ERR)
637:       let max = -Infinity
638:       for (const arg of args) {
639:         const v = this.getRangeValues(arg)
640:         if (v.some(x => x.isError())) {
641:           for (const val of v) {
642:             if (val.isError()) return val
643:           }
644:         }
645:         for (const val of v) {
646:           const num = val.asNumber()
647:           if (num.isError()) return num
648:           max = Math.max(max, num.val)
649:         }
650:       }
651:       return Value.number(max === -Infinity ? 0 : max)
652:     }
653: 
654:     if (name === 'COUNT') {
655:       if (args.length === 0) return Value.error(ERROR_ERR)
656:       let count = 0
657:       for (const arg of args) {
658:         const v = this.getRangeValues(arg)
659:         for (const val of v) {
660:           if (val.isError()) continue
661:           if (val.type === 'number') count++
662:         }
663:       }
664:       return Value.number(count)
665:     }
666: 
667:     if (name === 'AVG') {
668:       if (args.length === 0) return Value.error(ERROR_ERR)
669:       let sum = 0
670:       let count = 0
671:       for (const arg of args) {
672:         const v = this.getRangeValues(arg)
673:         if (v.some(x => x.isError())) {
674:           for (const val of v) {
675:             if (val.isError()) return val
676:           }
677:         }
678:         for (const val of v) {
679:           const num = val.asNumber()
680:           if (num.isError()) return num
681:           sum += num.val
682:           count++
683:         }
684:       }
685:       if (count === 0) return Value.number(0)
686:       return Value.number(sum / count)
687:     }
688: 
689:     if (name === 'ABS') {
690:       if (args.length !== 1) return Value.error(ERROR_ERR)
691:       const val = this.evaluateAst(args[0])
692:       if (val.isError()) return val
693:       const num = val.asNumber()
694:       if (num.isError()) return num
695:       return Value.number(Math.abs(num.val))
696:     }
697: 
698:     if (name === 'IF') {
699:       if (args.length !== 3) return Value.error(ERROR_ERR)
700:       const cond = this.evaluateAst(args[0])
701:       if (cond.isError()) return cond
702:       const isTruthy = cond.type === 'boolean' ? cond.val : cond.type === 'number' ? cond.val !== 0 : true
703:       if (isTruthy) {
704:         return this.evaluateAst(args[1])
705:       } else {
706:         return this.evaluateAst(args[2])
707:       }
708:     }
709: 
710:     return Value.error(ERROR_NAME)
711:   }
712: }

I rewrote the implementation under `src/` (`parser.js`, new `formula.js`, `evaluator.js`, `formatter.js`, `cli.js`). All 18 tests pass and no `node_modules` exists.

Bugs found and fixed against the specification:

- **Two-letter columns were mis-numbered.** `colToNum` computed `26 + (letter0 - 'A')` (and reconstructed labels as `'A' + …`), so every range and every ordering touching `AA`..`ZZ` was wrong. Now `AA`=26 … `ZZ`=701, with a matching inverse.
- **Literal `TRUE`/`FALSE` were read as booleans.** The spec's literal rules are: empty → 0, number, error token, everything else text. They are now text.
- **Unknown characters silently ended the formula.** `=1 @ 2` parsed as `1`; the tokenizer now rejects them, and also rejects malformed numbers such as `1.2.3` and `1.`.
- **A range inside parentheses counted as a direct argument.** Parentheses now build a node, so `SUM((A1:A2))` is `#ERR!` while `SUM(A1:A2)` is not.
- **Errors did not win over `#VALUE!` in calls.** Arguments are now fully expanded and scanned left to right for the first error before any number conversion, so `SUM(text, #REF!)` is `#REF!`.
- **`COUNT` ignored errors**; it now returns the first error among its values.
- **A range with an out-of-range endpoint contributed nothing**; it is now `#REF!`.
- **`IF` with a text condition returned the true branch**; text in a condition is now `#VALUE!`.
- **Extra arguments were accepted** (`cli.js values deps` exited 0); exactly one mode word is now required.
- Comparison of texts uses code points rather than UTF-16 code units, `process.exit` no longer risks truncating piped stdout, and `deps` no longer evaluates the sheet.
